value: 鋼の錬金術師 (Hagane no Renkinjutsushi)
text: The Japanese title is 鋼の錬金術師, read Hagane no Renkinjutsushi, which can be rendered as Alchemist of Steel.
excerpt: Fullmetal Alchemist (Japanese: 鋼の錬金術師, Hepburn: Hagane no Renkinjutsushi; lit. 'Alchemist of Steel')

value: Hiromu Arakawa (story and art)
text: Hiromu Arakawa wrote and drew the Fullmetal Alchemist manga all by herself.
excerpt: a Japanese manga series written and illustrated by Hiromu Arakawa

value: Monthly Shōnen Gangan, July 2001 to June 2010
text: Square Enix published the manga in its Monthly Shōnen Gangan magazine, from July 2001 until June 2010.
excerpt: serialized in Square Enix's shōnen manga anthology magazine Monthly Shōnen Gangan between July 2001 and June 2010

text: The finished story fills 27 collected volumes.
excerpt: the publisher later collected the individual chapters in 27 tankōbon volumes

value: over 90 million
text: Worldwide sales of the manga have passed 90 million copies.
excerpt: It has sold over 90 million copies worldwide

value: Shogakukan Manga Award (shōnen), 2004
text: In 2004 the manga won the 49th Shogakukan Manga Award in the shōnen category.
excerpt: It received the 49th Shogakukan Manga Award for the shōnen category in 2004

value: 51 episodes, 2003 to 2004
text: Studio Bones produced the first TV anime. Its 51 episodes were broadcast on the MBS and TBS networks, starting in October 2003 and finishing a year later.
excerpt: The anime series aired a total of 51 episodes on MBS, TBS and its affiliates from October 2003 to October 2004.

value: Seiji Mizushima (director), Shō Aikawa (writer), Michiru Ōshima (music)
text: Seiji Mizushima directed the 2003 anime, Shō Aikawa wrote it and Michiru Ōshima composed the score.
excerpt: The series was directed by Seiji Mizushima, written by Shō Aikawa, and musically composed by Michiru Ōshima.

value: original ending from about episode 12
text: Arakawa asked for an original ending, so the first anime left the manga plot after roughly a dozen episodes and told its own story.
excerpt: Arakawa requested a screenwriter-led original ending for the series that differed from the manga

value: 64 episodes, 2009 to 2010
text: The second anime, Brotherhood, was shown on MBS and TBS from spring 2009 to summer 2010 and adapts the whole manga story in 64 episodes.
excerpt: The series aired a total of 64 episodes on MBS, TBS and its affiliates from April 2009 to July 2010.

value: Yasuhiro Irie (director), Hiroshi Ōnogi (writer), Akira Senju (music)
text: Yasuhiro Irie directed Brotherhood, Hiroshi Ōnogi wrote it and Akira Senju composed the music, all at Bones.
excerpt: Produced by Bones, the series was directed by Yasuhiro Irie and written by Hiroshi Ōnogi, with music composed by Akira Senju.

value: Seiji Mizushima and Yasuhiro Irie
text: Two directors shaped the anime: Seiji Mizushima for the 2003 series and Yasuhiro Irie for Brotherhood.
excerpt: the series was directed by Yasuhiro Irie and written by Hiroshi Ōnogi
